title: The Rough Current
premise: Ada Okonkwo, a disgraced railroad engineer working off her father's debts on a colonial survey crew, is sent upriver to reopen a closed line to the highlands. When the expedition's radio goes silent and two porters vanish near the old tunnel works, Ada discovers the line was abandoned for reasons buried in her father's own survey notes. Guided by a rival engineer, Elias Vance, and a river pilot named Ngozi who knows the water better than any map, she pushes toward the forbidden source before the dry season strands them. At the source, Ada finds the truth: her father sabotaged the line to protect the valley from being flooded, and the debt she carries is the price of his silence. She must choose between completing the line as ordered—securing her name and future—and destroying her father's final survey to keep the river free, a choice that costs her career but gives her a home among the people of the current.
about_author: J. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent six years mapping river routes across West Africa before turning to fiction. Their novels blend engineering precision with a deep reverence for wild places and the people who call them home.

chapters.title: The Weight of Brass
chapters.summary: Ada Okonkwo arrives at the coastal rail depot, carrying her father's compass and a ledger of his debts. Her POV establishes her exile from the engineering corps and her desperate acceptance of the upriver assignment. The emotional beat is quiet humiliation sharpened into resolve: this expedition is her last chance to restore her name.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: In the survey office, Ada studies the sealed maps of the abandoned highland line and notices her father's initials on the original route. Told from her POV, the chapter builds unease as officials refuse to explain why the line closed twenty years ago. Beat: the first hook of inheritance—her past is already written into this journey.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Argues with Rivers
chapters.summary: Ada meets Ngozi, the sharp-tongued river pilot hired against her objections, and Elias Vance, the polished engineer assigned to oversee her. Alternating POVs show mutual distrust: Ngozi thinks Ada is another company man; Ada resents Elias's easy privilege. Beat: friction that will become loyalty.

chapters.title: Departure at First Light
chapters.summary: The expedition launches: three boats, twelve porters, radio equipment, and six weeks before the dry season closes the upper rapids. Ada's POV captures the mixture of dread and exhilaration on the water. Beat: point of no return—the city, and her old life, fall behind.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Ngozi threads the boats through the lower gorges while Ada learns the river's grammar—reading water like track gradients. A near-capsize forces Ada and Ngozi into their first real cooperation. Beat: grudging respect begins; the river becomes a character, beautiful and indifferent.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on the Map
chapters.summary: The crew shelters in a riverside village absent from official surveys. Through Ngozi's POV, we learn the villagers remember the rail crews—and remember Ada's father by name. Beat: Ada realizes her family history is entangled with places the company erased.

chapters.title: Static on the Wire
chapters.summary: The radio begins failing intermittently; base camp's replies grow garbled and then cease. Elias insists it's atmospheric interference; Ada suspects otherwise. His POV reveals he's carrying sealed orders he hasn't shared. Beat: isolation tightens, and trust fractures along hidden fault lines.

chapters.title: Two Porters Gone
chapters.summary: At dawn, two porters are missing along with a supply crate. Ada organizes the search herself, finding a torn company satchel near an overgrown cutting of the old line. Beat: fear curdles into suspicion—is someone in the party lying? The expedition's cohesion starts to crack.

chapters.title: Her Father's Numbers
chapters.summary: Cross-checking elevations, Ada discovers discrepancies between her father's original survey and the company's published figures—deliberate ones. Her POV chapter is a quiet revelation: he falsified data, but in which direction, and why? Beat: the debt she carries becomes a mystery she can't put down.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Rain
chapters.summary: A storm traps the crew under canvas. Ada accuses Elias of hiding orders; he deflects, but Ngozi sides with Ada, tipping the alliance. Elias's POV admits a sliver of truth: headquarters wants the source reached before anyone else. Beat: love against duty stirs—Elias's admiration for Ada wars with his obedience.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Works
chapters.summary: The expedition reaches the half-built tunnel where the old line died. Inside, Ada finds blasting charges never fired and a maintenance log in her father's hand, dated after the official closure. Beat: her father didn't abandon the project—he stayed secretly. The forbidden source draws closer.

chapters.title: Ngozi's Country
chapters.summary: Above the gorge, the river widens into country Ngozi knows intimately—her mother's people live upstream. Her POV chapter reveals what the flooding of the proposed reservoir would drown: villages, graves, a whole way of life. Beat: belonging reframed; Ada sees what 'progress' would cost.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone destroys one boat and most of the fuel overnight. With the radio dead and supplies halved, reaching the source and returning before the dry season seems impossible. Ada's POV chapter is cold arithmetic: someone wants them stopped—or wants only some of them to arrive. Beat: rising dread, dwindling options.

chapters.title: The Confession at the Fire
chapters.summary: Elias finally confesses: headquarters plans to blame the line's failure on Ada's father, posthumously, to justify a new dam scheme—and Elias was sent to verify the old survey's 'errors.' His POV breaks open with shame. Beat: betrayal transformed into choice; Elias asks Ada to let him help her instead.

chapters.title: Portage of Ghosts
chapters.summary: The crew hauls the remaining boat around the great falls through country the porters call haunted. Ada walks beside her father's ghost in memory, understanding at last why he carried this secret alone. Beat: grief and inheritance reconciled; the crew, tested, has become something like a family.

chapters.title: Dry Season Rising
chapters.summary: Water levels drop faster than expected; the return window shrinks to days. Ngozi warns they can go upstream or home—not both. Ada must decide whether to push on. Her POV weighs duty against everything she now knows. Beat: the ticking clock made physical; commitment despite the cost.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: A small party—Ada, Elias, Ngozi—reaches the source: a spring-fed basin where her father's final cache waits. Inside are his true surveys proving the dam's figures were falsified by the company itself. Beat: the climax of knowledge; the truth is in her hands, and it will ruin whoever holds it publicly.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Elias reveals the last twist: he was ordered to retrieve the cache and destroy it, with Ada's disappearance as cover. Instead he burns his own orders. His POV chapter is the surrender of duty to love. Beat: climax of character—he chooses her and the truth over his career.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Source
chapters.summary: Ada faces her decision: take the evidence downriver to certain scandal and probable suppression, or leave it hidden with the upstream villages who can reveal it when the time is right. She chooses the second, sealing her father's work into the valley's keeping. Beat: the thematic summit—belonging chosen over redemption on the company's terms.

chapters.title: Running the Falling Water
chapters.summary: The desperate descent: low water, damaged boat, rapids harder than anything they ran coming up. Ngozi's finest hour at the helm; Ada and Elias bailing and hauling. Beat: pure adventure catharsis—the river that threatened to keep them finally lets them go.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: At the coast, Ada delivers her report—stripped of the cache but damning in its own careful language—knowing it ends her career. Elias corroborates her and resigns. Beat: quiet sacrifice; the debt is paid not in money but in truth told plainly.

chapters.title: Where the Current Begins
chapters.summary: Months later, Ada returns upriver as a teacher of surveying for the valley communities, her compass finally her own. Ngozi pilots her home waters; Elias writes from afar, promising to come when the season turns. Beat: resolution—inheritance reclaimed, love patient, belonging found where the river begins.
